devices.source: MB85RS2MTA-DS6v1-E.pdf, DC table, PDF p.13 (IDD @40 MHz: 1.9 typ / 2.3 max)
devices.note: single operating-current row applied to read and write; VDD 3.3 V column; "takes no wait time"

devices.name: Everspin MR25H10 (MRAM)
devices.source: MR25H10 Rev. 9.5 (3/2018), Table 3.4, PDF p.12 (distributor copy, not the vendor site)

excluded.name: Winbond W25Q64PW (NOR flash, 1.8 V)
excluded.reason: Needs erase before program and programs in <=256 B pages; not a byte-granular atomic-log medium. Reference numbers: program 8 mA typ x 1.8 V x 0.12 ms typ = 1.73 uJ per page (6.75 nJ/B if full; write ratio ~3.4x G6); 4 KB sector erase 30 ms typ x 8 mA x 1.8 V = 432 uJ (105 nJ/B amortised; ratio ~53x, beyond the grid). W25Q64PW Rev D, DC table PDF p.66, AC p.69.

rule: range = [min, max] over included devices, typ and max conditions, of device_energy/G6_coefficient for read and write separately; byte-addressable no-erase NVM only
limitations: Chip-only lower bound; SPI master/IO, level shifting, controller, converter, startup are not included.
One scale multiplies read and write equally; G6 write/read = 2 while FRAM ~1 and MRAM ~3.8, so no single scale matches every device.
MR25H10 figures come from a distributor copy of Rev 9.5; MB85RS2MTA assumes the same IDD for read and write.
On-chip embedded NVM (far lower pJ/byte) and flash with erase (far higher) are outside this range and outside the verdict.
